answer: A burst of registrations as a result prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. The velvet multiplier is published, charged in vine, and relic lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 11 for every identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. A farm of 1710 identities would post 4947 proofs and burn roughly 2 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
